awd_titl_txt: I-Corps: Translation Potential of a Smart Retractor to Enhance Surgical Procedures
awd_abstract_narration:
The broader impact/commercial potential of this I-Corps project is the development of an advanced surgical tool designed to improve patient safety and reduce complications during surgery. The project focuses on creating a device that integrates real-time monitoring and enhanced visualization to prevent tissue damage that causes Mastectomy Skin Flap Necrosis, a devastating complication for breast cancer patients. This technology can be applied across a wide range of surgical procedures beyond mastectomies, potentially reducing the incidence of complications, minimizing the need for additional surgeries, and lowering overall healthcare costs. By addressing a critical need for improved surgical precision, this project aims to enhance overall patient outcomes and reduce healthcare expenses, positioning the technology as a valuable asset in medical settings with broad implications for improving surgical practices and patient care.

This I-Corps project utilizes experiential learning coupled with a first-hand investigation of the industry ecosystem to assess the translation potential of the technology. This solution is based on the development of a surgical retractor equipped with sensors that continuously monitor retraction levels and provide real-time feedback to surgeons. The technology integrates a miniature camera to enhance visualization, similar to an endoscope, and relies on data-driven algorithms to assess safe pressure ranges. Preliminary research has demonstrated the retractor's capability to identify retraction levels and alert surgeons before excessive pressure causes tissue damage. By integrating these features, the technology offers a novel approach to preventing complications and advancing surgical practices.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This project explored the translation potential of a “smart retractor,” a novel surgical tool designed to improve safety and outcomes during operations. The technology addresses a critical challenge in breast cancer surgery: preventing tissue damage that can occur when skin is stretched during procedures, which may lead to complications requiring additional surgeries.

The intellectual merit of this project lies in advancing understanding of how real-time data and visualization can improve surgical precision. The team developed and evaluated a concept for a retractor equipped with sensors that measure retraction force and provide feedback to surgeons, along with enhanced visualization capabilities similar to a miniature camera. These features support safer decision-making during surgery by helping surgeons avoid excessive pressure and better assess tissue health. Through over 100 stakeholder interviews, operating room observations, and engagement with surgeons and hospital leaders, the project validated that improved visualization and intraoperative feedback are key unmet needs in surgical oncology.

The broader impacts of the project are substantial. The proposed technology has the potential to reduce complications such as skin flap necrosis, which affects a significant portion of patients undergoing mastectomy procedures and often leads to increased healthcare costs and patient distress. By enabling earlier detection of unsafe conditions during surgery, the system could reduce unnecessary follow-up procedures, improve patient outcomes, and lower costs for hospitals and insurers. In addition, the project contributed to workforce and educational development. The device concept can be adapted for training purposes, offering real-time feedback that helps medical trainees build surgical skills more effectively and safely. The project also provided hands-on entrepreneurial training for the research team, building expertise in customer discovery, healthcare systems, and commercialization strategy.

Overall, this award established a strong foundation for translating an innovative surgical technology from concept toward real-world application, with the potential to improve patient care across multiple types of surgeries.
